protein: Fks1, the catalytic subunit of 1,3-beta-glucan synthase; variants are site-saturated across hotspot 1 (residues 639 to 647)
readout: Selection coefficient in bulk competition without drug, on the scale of the median silent mutant of this library (wild type expected near 0)
assay_method: Pooled bulk competition of a genome-edited NNK site-saturation library covering hotspot 1 (residues 639 to 647) of FKS1 at its endogenous locus in S. cerevisiae BY4741, without drug, sampled before and after two consecutive rounds of selection and read by amplicon deep sequencing of the hotspot; three biological replicates. The selection coefficient is a log-ratio of allele frequencies normalized by the number of mitotic generations, counted by flow cytometry, and by the median log2 fold-change of silent mutants excluding the wild-type nucleotide sequence, which is overabundant by oPool design. Drug concentrations were set to inhibit about 80 percent of wild-type growth.
remark: 9 rows carrying a premature stop codon are dropped, a nonsense variant having no substitution label in this format, and 5 substitutions the paper also reports (F639C, L640D, L642G, P647N, P647Q) are absent because they were missing from the pooled library and were measured individually in validation growth assays instead. V641W and L642K keep their pooled-competition values, whereas the authors' classification tables replace both with individual validation estimates they judge less biased, the two diverging most under micafungin at 0.081 here against 0.574 there. Figure 2d counts 76 hotspot 1 single mutants resistant to all three echinocandins, which reproduces exactly from the deposited classification table; 72 of them are in this file, the remainder being the nonsense variant S643* and three of the individually measured substitutions. Also measured in the same file and not curated here: the same hotspot libraries in the R1158 background with FKS2 repressible by doxycycline, and two FKS2 hotspot libraries, each a separately normalized screen; the homolog hotspot libraries shipped alongside are excluded, being natural FKS sequences from other species rather than variants of one wild type. The paper counts 465 Fks1 single mutants confidently classified as sensitive or resistant across the three hotspots; recounting unique amino-acid variants classified in at least one drug from the deposited classification tables gives 462, and the 3-variant gap is unexplained.

protein: CbbM, the form II rubisco of Gallionella sp.; variants are built on a pre-engineering parent two substitutions from the wild-type enzyme, and carry an N-terminal Strep-tag
readout: Normalized weighted mean fitness under constant light, oxygen-free, on the source's scale where the parent is 1.0 and the median K214 substitution, which abolishes catalysis, is the intended zero
assay_method: Growth-coupled selection in Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 carrying a CRISPR-interference knockdown of its endogenous rubisco, so growth rate reports the activity of the heterologous CbbM. A barcoded library of the variants was grown in turbidostat mode for about ten generations in eight replicates under constant light at 300 uE with 5 percent CO2, 95 percent N2 and no O2, with samples taken for Illumina sequencing throughout; fitness is a weighted mean over the barcodes of each variant. The library saturates 67 positions with every other amino acid and varies a further seven combinatorially, two positions belonging to both, for 72 mutated positions in all.
remark: The sequence is the assayed construct, 484 residues including the N-terminal Strep-tag and linker MWSHPQFEKGSGSG, because the source states that its numbering is based on the tagged sequence and all 1225 distinct substitution labels verify against it with no offset. The row labelled WT is not wild-type CbbM but the library's parent, which the source describes as two amino acid exchanges from the wild-type Gallionella enzyme and calls WT for simplicity; against UniProt D9SHP6, the 470-residue rubisco of Gallionella capsiferriformans ES-2, the untagged construct differs at six positions, of which the source accounts for two as the engineered exchanges and the remainder are presumably isolate differences that cannot be resolved from what is deposited. Of the 39386 rows in the source table only 13966 carry a measurement, the rest being variants scored by the paper's models but never built, and a further 32 rows are dropped because their label carries a STOP token, a truncation having no substitution form in this format. The readout is the source's own normalized weighted mean fitness and is used unchanged; its zero point is the median K214 substitution rather than a non-growing control, K214 being the carbamylated lysine required for catalysis, so a variant scoring below 0 is by the source's own reading catalytically dead; the parent lands at exactly 1.000 in all three conditions but the median of the 18 K214 substitutions lands at +0.0109 rather than exactly zero in this table, a small residual the source does not explain. The article PDF is not redistributed in papers/: Science Advances blocks direct retrieval and the PMC record the DOI resolver advertises returns 404, so the datasets are built from the authors' GitHub deposit, which the paper's figure-by-figure index in its README ties to the published figures. Not extracted from this paper: the EVmutation, DeepSequence, MSA-Transformer, ProteinNPT and additive columns of the same table, which are computed predictions rather than measurements.
